modality: SAR (Sentinel-1) & Optical (Sentinel-2) GeoTIFFs + Binary Masks
spatial_coverage: Global (11 major flood events across 6 continents, 4,831 chips)
access_method: Google Cloud Storage (gsutil cp -r gs://sen1floods11) / GitHub repo scripts
flood_ai_phase: Phase 1: SAR Flood Segmentation Model Training
primary_use_case: Train and benchmark deep learning flood segmentation models (e.g., U-Net/SegFormer) on all-weather Sentinel-1 SAR imagery.
key_limitations: Only 446 hand-labeled chips (rest are weakly labeled); static event snapshots rather than continuous time-series.

modality: Multispectral Optical (Sentinel-2) GeoTIFFs + Flood Masks
access_method: GitHub repository & Google Cloud Storage / GEE export scripts
registration_required: No (GEE registration if exporting custom scenes)
flood_ai_phase: Phase 1: Optical Flood Mapping & Cross-Modal Fusion
primary_use_case: Optical water-index (NDWI/MNDWI) flood detection and multimodal fusion with Sen1Floods11 SAR features.
recommended_pilot_cities: Global (clear-sky validation for Dhaka, Houston, Manila)
key_limitations: Heavily degraded by dense cloud cover during active storms and cyclones.

modality: Very High Resolution (VHR) Optical Satellite Imagery + JSON Building Polygons
spatial_coverage: Global (19 disaster events, including Hurricane Harvey/Florence/Midwest floods; >850,000 building polygons)
access_method: xView2 portal download & GitHub preprocessing scripts
registration_required: Yes (Free account on xView2 / DARPA portal)
flood_ai_phase: Phase 3: Post-Event Structural Damage & Impact Estimation
primary_use_case: Train building localization and 4-level structural damage classification models (no damage to destroyed) for flood impact scoring.
key_limitations: Mixed disaster types (requires filtering for flood/hurricane events); optical VHR imagery is costly to acquire in real time.

modality: Tabular CSV / Structured Features & Flood Labels
access_method: Kaggle CLI (kaggle datasets download -d floodml/floodml) or Kaggle Web UI
registration_required: Yes (Free Kaggle account & API token kaggle.json)
flood_ai_phase: Phase 2: Rapid Baseline ML Prototyping
primary_use_case: Fast prototyping and baseline benchmarking of tabular flood risk classifiers (XGBoost/LightGBM/MLP) before full geospatial fusion.
key_limitations: Not a live operational feed; lacks raw geospatial rasters for pixel-level inundation mapping.

modality: Gridded NetCDF / GRIB Climate Reanalysis
spatial_resolution: 0.25 deg (~31 km); ERA5-Land at 0.1 deg (~9 km)
approx_size: Petabytes total (~100 MB - 5 GB per pilot city multi-year query)
access_method: Copernicus Climate Data Store Python API (cdsapi) or Web UI
flood_ai_phase: Phase 2: Historical Hydro-Meteorological Model Training
primary_use_case: Extract historical rainfall, soil moisture, runoff, surface pressure, and wind features to train spatio-temporal flood forecasting models.
key_limitations: ~5-day release lag prevents real-time nowcasting; coarse ~31 km grid misses localized urban flash-flood cells.

modality: Gridded Satellite Precipitation (HDF5 / NetCDF / GeoTIFF)
approx_size: Terabytes total (~50 MB - 2 GB per storm event/region)
access_method: NASA Earthdata HTTPS/OPeNDAP, GES DISC Python scripts, or GEE
flood_ai_phase: Phase 2: Near-Real-Time Rainfall Ingestion & Nowcasting
primary_use_case: Near-real-time high-frequency rainfall accumulation tracking across data-sparse basins (especially Asia/tropics).
key_limitations: 4-hour latency on Early Run; reduced accuracy over extreme mountainous terrain or very light rain.

modality: Doppler Weather Radar (Level II & Level III binary / NetCDF)
spatial_coverage: United States & territories (160 WSR-88D radar sites)
approx_size: Petabytes total (~500 MB - 5 GB per storm event)
access_method: NOAA NCEI Archive / AWS Open Data S3 (s3://noaa-nexrad-level2) via boto3/Py-ART
flood_ai_phase: Phase 2: Ultra-High-Resolution Urban Flash Flood Nowcasting
primary_use_case: Sub-kilometer real-time storm cell tracking and rainfall rate estimation for US urban flash flood alerts.
key_limitations: US coverage only; radar data requires specialized preprocessing (clutter filtering, Z-R conversion via Py-ART).

modality: JSON REST API (Current, Hourly 48h, Daily 8d forecasts & alerts)
temporal_coverage: Real-time + up to 8-day forecast (historical requires paid tier)
access_method: HTTP REST API (Python requests to One Call API 3.0 / Current Weather)
registration_required: Yes (Free API key with call limits; paid tiers for bulk/history)
flood_ai_phase: Phase 2 & 4: Live Operational Dashboard & 72h Forecast Feed
primary_use_case: Ingest live rainfall rate, forecast precipitation, humidity, and government weather alerts for the real-time siren dashboard.
key_limitations: Free tier rate limits; point-based forecasts lack fine spatial hydrology detail compared to radar/satellite grids.

modality: Time-Series Tabular (WaterML / JSON / RDB)
spatial_resolution: Point gauge stations (~11,000+ active US streamgages)
access_method: USGS NWIS Water Services REST API (https://waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/iv/) or Python dataretrieval package
flood_ai_phase: Phase 2: River Stage & Discharge Forecasting (LSTM/TFT)
primary_use_case: Stream live 15-minute river stage (gage height) and discharge (cfs) to calibrate danger thresholds and train hydrographs.
key_limitations: US coverage only; individual gauges may experience sensor outages or ice/debris interference during extreme floods.

modality: Station Water Level Tables / Bulletins (HTML / CSV / PDF via FFWC)
spatial_resolution: Point river gauge stations (~100+ flood monitoring stations)
access_method: Web portal / Flood Forecasting & Warning Centre (FFWC) bulletins & official data request
registration_required: No for public bulletins (Formal request required for bulk historical archives)
flood_ai_phase: Phase 2: Local River Stage Calibration & Danger Level Triggers
primary_use_case: Provide ground-truth water levels and official Danger Level (DL) marks for Dhaka and surrounding Bangladesh rivers.
key_limitations: No standardized public REST API; requires web scraping/parsing or formal agency access for long historical series.

modality: River Gauge Bulletins & Flood Forecast Tables (HTML / JSON / PDF)
spatial_resolution: Point gauge stations (~300+ flood forecasting stations across India)
access_method: CWC Flood Forecasting portal (ffs.india-water.gov.in) / CWC website & India-WRIS portal
registration_required: No for public flood bulletins (Registration/request for bulk historical datasets)
flood_ai_phase: Phase 2: River Stage Thresholding & India Pilot Calibration
primary_use_case: Obtain official Warning Level, Danger Level, and Highest Flood Level (HFL) benchmarks for Indian river basins.
recommended_pilot_cities: Indian pilot cities (e.g., Mumbai, Guwahati, Patna)
key_limitations: Limited open programmatic API; some transboundary basin data is classified/restricted.

modality: River Discharge Time-Series (ASCII / CSV / NetCDF) + Station Shapefiles
spatial_resolution: Point gauge stations (>10,000 stations in 159 countries)
access_method: GRDC Data Portal (portal.grdc.bafg.de) interactive selection & download
flood_ai_phase: Phase 2: Cross-Basin Hydrological Baseline & Model Validation
primary_use_case: Historical discharge baselines and return-period flood statistics for global basins lacking open national APIs.
key_limitations: Not real-time (multi-month to multi-year lag); uneven station density and temporal gaps in developing regions.

modality: Gridded Population Density Rasters (GeoTIFF)
access_method: Direct HTTPS/FTP download, WorldPop REST API, or Google Earth Engine
flood_ai_phase: Phase 3: Population-at-Risk & Impact Scoring
primary_use_case: Overlay predicted flood inundation masks with 100m population grids to compute exact population at risk per hotspot.
key_limitations: Static residential population (does not capture daytime/nighttime commuting shifts); relies on census disaggregation.

modality: Vector Data (OSM XML / PBF / GeoJSON)
spatial_resolution: Building, road, and waterway vector precision (~1-5m)
approx_size: ~75 GB global PBF (~50 MB - 1 GB per city/country extract)
access_method: Overpass API, Python OSMnx library, or Geofabrik/BBBike regional PBF extracts
flood_ai_phase: Phase 3 & 4: Evacuation Routing, Critical Infrastructure & Base Map
primary_use_case: Extract road networks for safe evacuation corridors, locate hospitals/shelters, and map river/canal geometries.
key_limitations: Crowdsourced completeness varies in rural/informal settlements; road elevation/floodability attributes are often missing.

modality: Gridded Built-Up Surface, Volume & Settlement Rasters (GeoTIFF)
approx_size: ~50 MB - 2 GB per regional tile (100m); larger at 10m
access_method: European Commission JRC GHSL Download Portal (HTTP/Python wget) or GEE
flood_ai_phase: Phase 3: Urban Density & Built-Environment Exposure
primary_use_case: Distinguish dense urban cores from rural floodplains and quantify exposed built-up area/building volume.
key_limitations: 5-year update intervals miss rapid informal urban expansion; does not distinguish building structural materials.

modality: Vector Shapefiles / GeoPackage (Physical & Cultural layers)
access_method: Direct ZIP download from Natural Earth website or GitHub
flood_ai_phase: Phase 1 & 4: Regional Boundary Clipping & Overview Maps
primary_use_case: Provide clean country/admin boundaries, coastlines, and major river centerlines for UI framing and regional clipping.
key_limitations: Too coarse for street-level urban flood mapping; use OpenStreetMap for city-scale geometry.

modality: Multimodal Social Media (Tweet Text TSV + Disaster Images JPEG)
temporal_resolution: Event-based (7 major disasters including Hurricanes Harvey/Irma/Maria & Sri Lanka floods)
spatial_coverage: Multi-country disaster events (~18,000 labeled tweets & images)
access_method: GitHub repository / CrisisNLP portal ZIP download
flood_ai_phase: Phase 4: Multimodal Social Media Verification Classifier
primary_use_case: Train multimodal text+image classifiers to separate informative flood eyewitness reports and damage severity from noise.
key_limitations: English-dominated; limited to 2017 events; sparse GPS coordinates require Named Entity Recognition (NER) geoparsing.

modality: Labeled Disaster Tweets (TSV text + humanitarian categories)
spatial_coverage: Global (includes floods, hurricanes, cyclones across multiple countries)
access_method: GitHub repository / CrisisNLP download (tweet IDs + text splits)
flood_ai_phase: Phase 4: Humanitarian Need & Rescue Triage NLP
primary_use_case: Fine-tune transformer NLP models to classify live posts into rescue requests, displaced people, infrastructure damage, and shelter needs.
key_limitations: Text-only (no images); primarily English; class imbalance across rare humanitarian categories.

modality: Real-Time JSON Stream / Search API (Text, Media URLs, Geotags)
spatial_resolution: Point / Bounding-box geotags (sparse) + text location mentions
access_method: X API v2 REST / Filtered Stream via Python Tweepy or requests
registration_required: Yes (Developer account; Paid Basic/Pro tier required for practical read/search volume)
flood_ai_phase: Phase 4: Live Crowdsourced Ground-Truth & Alert Verification
primary_use_case: Ingest live local flood eyewitness posts and feed them into CrisisMMD/HumAID-trained models to verify real-time street inundation.
key_limitations: Strict rate limits and high API pricing on Free/Basic tiers; <2% of posts carry exact GPS coordinates; high noise/misinformation.

modality: Cloud Platform hosting Raster/Vector catalogs (Sentinel-1/2, ERA5, GPM, WorldPop, GHSL)
approx_size: Petabyte-scale cloud catalog (zero local storage until export)
access_method: GEE Python API (earthengine-api / geemap) or JavaScript Code Editor
registration_required: Yes (Free for research, education, and non-commercial humanitarian projects)
flood_ai_phase: All Phases: Server-Side Preprocessing, Feature Extraction & Tile Export
primary_use_case: Server-side SAR/Optical compositing, cloud masking, ERA5/GPM/WorldPop spatial alignment, and exporting ML-ready patches without downloading terabytes.
key_limitations: Export size/memory quotas per task; requires Google Cloud Project linking; non-commercial licensing restrictions for free tier.
